title: TwoLeadECG redundant Q.ANT readout robustness test
research_question: Can redundant independent Q.ANT Fourier/KAN readout heads reduce reference/Q.ANT prediction disagreements on TwoLeadECG without materially reducing Q.ANT accuracy?
hypothesis: Averaging three independently parameterized Q.ANT-compatible 80→2 Fourier/KAN heads during both training and inference will reduce sensitivity to small distributed numerical perturbations compared with the single-head control.
rationale: Exp014 localized disagreements near tiny decision margins, Exp015 found a generic margin penalty ineffective, and Exp016 found no dominant local error source. Redundant readout tests whether averaging multiple Q.ANT-native decision paths can suppress distributed numerical perturbations.

candidates.redundant3: three independently parameterized Q.ANT Fourier/KAN heads 80→2; arithmetic mean of logits in reference and Q.ANT inference

success_criteria: Supported if redundant3 has strictly fewer mean reference/Q.ANT disagreements than control and mean Q.ANT accuracy >= control - 0.01.
promotion_rule: No automatic PNN-v1 promotion. If supported, validate redundant readout on another transfer dataset before architectural promotion.
hardware_boundary: Q.ANT CPU/software simulation only; no physical photonic hardware performance claim.
